propositions: A newly added hard-fail CI gate breaks branches created before the gate was added, because the code-review gate lacks a criterion checking whether gate changes would break in-flight branches.

An advisory project code-review criterion project.ci-gate-compat should be added to ask CI-agnostically whether a pipeline/gate-configuration change introduces a hard-fail step or required gate with no grandfather guard.
Project code-review criteria are currently dispatched unconditionally without checking their applies_to glob patterns against changed files, preventing glob-based filtering from working.
The applies_to glob set must be overridable per-project via a config key code_review.ci_config_globs so unusual pipelines are declared rather than hard-coded.

Criteria routing applies_to globs must be CI-vendor-agnostic and declarative, covering multiple CI systems via glob patterns rather than hard-coded Python vendor checks, so adding a CI system requires only adding a glob.
The operator rejected the criterion as institutionalizing workaround behavior instead of fixing gate failures, and this ticket must close unimplemented.
